title: Baluchari sari
summary: Baluchari saris are silk cloths of Bengal, traditionally woven on a frame loom in deep, dark colours. Extra silk threads float over the surface in long smooth lines, making leaves, flowers and paisley shapes in the border and the end piece of the cloth. The floats lie flat and glossy, like satin.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other side of the centre line.
Copy the panel shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The panel is mirrored left and right, so every shape you place also appears on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the pattern you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: The cloth is named for Baluchar in the Murshidabad region of Bengal, and weaving of this kind is also linked with the town of Bishnupur. Weavers set the designs in the loom by hand, thread by thread, so a single end piece can take many days.
